enforcement_note: A formatter enforces layout and a linter finds unused names; neither can tell whether a name reveals intent or whether an abstraction earned its place. Duplication detectors find identical text, not the same decision expressed twice.
rule: Audit naming, function shape, duplication and complexity, as questions.
ai_action: Work through the checklist against the code in question. Report the answers, including the ones that pass -- a checklist that only ever surfaces problems reads as noise. Where an answer is 'I cannot tell from here', say so rather than assuming the safe answer.

checklist.question: Does the name say what it is for rather than what it is made of?
Does the codebase already have a different word for this same concept?
checklist.remediation_hint: Adopt the existing term; two words for one thing invites a bug.

checklist.question: Can you describe what it does without saying 'and'?
checklist.group_condition: When adding or changing a function

checklist.question: Does a boolean parameter mean this is really two functions?
checklist.group_condition: When adding or changing a function

checklist.question: Does the body stay at one level of abstraction?
checklist.remediation_hint: Extract the lower-level steps behind named helpers.
checklist.group_condition: When adding or changing a function

checklist.question: Is this the same decision expressed twice, or merely similar text?
checklist.remediation_hint: Only the former is worth unifying.
checklist.group_condition: When similar code appears more than once

checklist.question: If this rule changed, how many files must change together?
checklist.remediation_hint: That count is the real cost; reduce it.
checklist.group_condition: When similar code appears more than once

checklist.question: Is there a layer here that exists in case something changes?
Does each comment say why, leaving what to the code?
checklist.remediation_hint: Delete comments that restate the line below.

anti_pattern: Do not convert these questions into prescriptions. A question makes you look at the code and survives a codebase it was not written for; a prescription tells you what to type and stops being right the moment the context differs.
